text: Case open!
Hey! That's not fair! Ivy didn't count!
I didn't need to. I just saw it.
Today's case: ladybird dots at a glance.
At a glance means one quick look.
Like the dots on a dice.
Mabel painted this ladybird stepping stone.
How many dots does it have?
I'll count. One, two, three, four, five!
Hmm. I saw four at a glance.
Four? You guessed!
Let's not guess. Let's test.
Can you point to the dots?
How many dots? Take a quick look.
A. Five dots.
B. Four dots.
Pause and think.
You can see small groups without counting.
Two dots on this wing.
Two dots on that wing.
Two and two make four.
It's B! Four dots.
Oh! I touched one dot twice!
Let's check another way.
Touch each dot only once.
One, two, three, four.
Four! Same as my quick look!
Case solved!
Hello, tiny ladybird! Can you count?
Ladybirds can't count, Otto!
Remember. You can see small groups without counting.
Say it with me. You can see small groups without counting.
Try it at home. Roll a dice. Say the number fast!
Next case: the shuffled clue cards.
